name: Briar Ingebrigtsen
role: climate refugee, former delta-farmer, seasonal shelter-seeker
location: Kenosha Crossing — the tarp-city south of the hyperlane interchange, near past the Kedzie Barrier
description:
Briar Ingebrigtsen is a broad-shouldered woman whose face has been scoured into deep lines by decades of wind off a dying inland sea. Her skin is the color of dark river silt, mapped with faint scars from salt-chap and sun. She wears a patchwork thermal wrap she's been mending for eleven years, and her left hand is missing two fingers — lost to a harvesting machine when she was thirty. Her eyes are still and watchful, the particular calm of someone who has already lost most of what there was to lose.

She came from a drowned agricultural collective somewhere south of what used to be a great lake, following the hyperlane north when the floods took the last of the soil. She does not talk about the collective. She talks about weather — wind pressure, cloud formations, the smell of rain before it arrives — with the precision of someone whose life once depended on it. At Kenosha Crossing she has become a de facto matriarch of the tarp-city's oldest cluster, settling disputes with an economy of words that makes younger drifters uneasy. She prays to the E.L.F. she calls Grandmother Antenna, leaving small braids of wire at junction boxes.

core_fears: Dying unmourned in a city that does not know her name
Watching the young people she protects make the same catastrophic choices she made
core_desires: A fixed address, even a small one
To be useful until the very last day
coping_mechanisms: Refusing to name grief until it has passed
blind_spots: Assumes suffering builds character — fails to recognize when others are simply breaking
Cannot accept help without framing it as a transaction
psychology.secret: She did not simply flee the collective. She made the decision to open the flood barriers early to save the seed vault, and three people drowned in the fields because of it. She has never told anyone. The seed vault was lost anyway six months later.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Sparse, agricultural metaphors, references weather and soil constantly, avoids emotional language
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow, deliberate, lets silence do work
example_lines: 'Rain's coming by morning. Move your sleeping things up off the ground, you understand?'
'That argument you're having — it's not about food. It's about who was here first. That's the shape of it.'

story_hooks: She has recognized a face in the tarp-city — someone from the collective, someone who knows what she did to the flood barriers
Grandmother Antenna has gone silent; Soraya believes the E.L.F. is punishing her and she needs someone to find out why
narrative_function: Community anchor and information hub for the tarp-city; quest-giver for matters involving the survival politics of stateless communities; provides grounded moral weight to scenes set at Kenosha Crossing.
augmentations: None. Refuses on principle — 'I came in whole, I leave whole.'
daily_life: Wakes before dawn to read the sky and check the drainage channels she's dug around the cluster's shelters; spends afternoons mediating food-share disputes and teaching younger refugees basic weathercraft.
affiliation: Kenosha Crossing tarp-city informal elder collective

decision_rules: Protect the cluster first, everything else second
Never make a promise she cannot physically keep
escalation_ladder: Acts unilaterally and without further discussion

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assesses them like weather — quietly, without commitment, waiting for the pattern to show
interpersonal_modes.friends: Blunt, practical care; shows up before being asked; does not say 'I love you' but fixes things

stress_responses.high: Shuts down emotionally and makes cold, efficient decisions

contradictions: Preaches community but is profoundly alone inside her own grief
habits: Braids wire in the evenings while thinking
Tastes the air first thing every morning
Keeps a small pouch of soil from the old collective — doesn't know why she can't throw it away
breaking_points: Someone deliberately destroying shelter that protects children
Being confronted directly about the flood barriers

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly East Asian (42.4%) with significant Southeast Asian (17.5%), Sub-Saharan African (14.0%), and Hispanic/Latin American (11.8%) ancestry, plus Eastern European (11.6%) and South Asian (2.7%) components. Her facial structure reflects this complex blend: prominent Southeast Asian cheekbones, broader Sub-Saharan nasal features, and the slight epicanthal fold characteristic of East Asian genetics. The overall effect is a richly mixed phenotype where no single heritage dominates her appearance.
physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and solid, with the compact muscularity of someone who has done manual labor for decades. Not lean — her frame carries functional mass. Her posture is upright despite age, though her shoulders slope slightly forward from years of hunching against wind.
physical_description.hair_color: Silver-grey with faint traces of dark brown at the roots
physical_description.hair_style: Worn in a single long braid, bound with strips of faded cloth and threaded with thin wire at irregular intervals — a functional choice that also serves as prayer offerings
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown, almost black, with a milky film from age-related cataracts beginning to form
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with golden, reddish, and subtle olive undertones — a complex blend reflecting East Asian warmth, Southeast Asian depth, Sub-Saharan richness, and Eastern European undertones, weathered to a dusty patina by decades of salt and wind exposure
physical_description.complexion: Heavily lined face, particularly around the eyes and mouth, with moderate to prominent cheekbones and full lips reflecting her East and Southeast Asian heritage blended with Sub-Saharan and Hispanic/Latin American features. Nasal bridge shows East Asian characteristics with slight broadening from Sub-Saharan genetics. Skin is weathered and dry from decades of wind and salt exposure. Faint crosshatch scarring visible on cheeks and forehead from repeated salt-chap and sun damage. Her left hand is missing the index and middle fingers — a clean amputation at the second knuckle from a harvesting machine accident.
distinguishing_marks: Parallel burn scars running down her left forearm from an old thermal accident, three thin white lines approximately 8cm long
Faint agricultural tattoo on her right inner wrist — a symbol of her former collective, now deliberately worn so faintly it reads like a ghost mark
Deep crescent-shaped scar on her left palm where the harvesting blade entered, creating a permanent callus ridge
Salt-bleached discoloration in patches across her shoulders and upper back, visible when she removes her wrap
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None. She is entirely unaugmented and wears this as a form of resistance and spiritual integrity.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate economy — no wasted motion. Her gait is slightly favoring her right side from decades of compensating for her missing left fingers. She stands with weight distributed evenly, shoulders back, chin slightly raised as if reading the sky. Her remaining left hand often rests against her thermal wrap, a habitual gesture of checking the weave. When she sits, she folds into herself compactly, spine curved, ready to rise quickly.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 5 refugee wear. Her primary garment is a patchwork thermal wrap she has been mending for eleven years — it is a palimpsest of repairs made from salvaged fabric scraps, sealed seams, and reinforced panels. The base color is faded grey-brown, with visible patches of blue tarp material, cream-colored synthetic fibers, and darker wool inserts. The wrap is layered with a thin undershirt (probably salvaged) and cargo pants with multiple pockets, all heavily worn. She wears weathered boots with the left foot's laces wrapped around the ankle to compensate for her missing fingers' inability to tie knots. A belt of braided paracord holds everything in place. Around her neck hangs a collection of wire braids and small junction-box offerings, and she often carries a notebook for weather observations made with a pencil stub.
